problem: VLN agents show a large seen/unseen performance gap because training environments are limited, and retraining on all seen data whenever new environments arrive is costly. Prior continual-learning work for VLN only tackles catastrophic forgetting and ignores improving generalization to unfamiliar environments.
motivation: Real-world agents encounter an ever-changing stream of scenes and must adapt to new ones while retaining old knowledge. Expanding datasets to cover more environments is impractical and expensive, so continual learning is proposed as an alternative to improve generalization.
key_idea: Dual-loop scenario replay: an inner loop trains on new-domain data mixed with randomly replayed samples from a per-scene memory buffer, and a Reptile-style outer meta-update interpolates weights to balance old and new knowledge.
insight: Replay plus meta-update lets the agent both resist forgetting and gain on unseen scenes, whereas plain fine-tuning collapses. In the ST/UT table, Dual-SR gets UT +2.18 on Val Unseen versus -8.03 for fine-tuning, and ST -6.00 versus -10.59 on Val Seen. Table 4 shows the fine-tune minimum SR on Val Seen is 5.83, versus 18.75 for Dual-SR. No ablation of the inner or outer loop or of the buffer is reported.
method: VLNCL paradigm: R2R is split into per-scene task domains (55 Train Seen, 53 Val Seen, 8 Val Unseen) that are fed sequentially to a pretrained base agent.

Inner loop (working memory): each new-domain batch is combined with rs samples randomly replayed from the buffer, with a per-parameter learnable learning rate α (element-wise) for the gradient update.
Outer loop (long-term memory): Reptile meta-update θ ← θ + β(θ' − θ) after each task domain, to reduce overfitting to single-scene data and improve generalization.
Multi-scenario memory buffer: organized by task domain, with equal chance of sampling each former domain; buffer size Z, and one task in a domain is replaced when the task ID is a multiple of Z.

Structured transformer planner (DUET/HAMT/TD-STP-like): global, candidate-target (5x5 grid, 6 m spacing), history, instruction and vision tokens; graph-masked attention; local and global action space; loss = IL + RL + history-teacher + target-prediction.
Metrics: Seen Transfer (ST, backward-transfer-like) and Unseen Transfer (UT, forward-transfer-like) computed on SR, with the unseen domain set shrinking as domains are encountered.

setting.backbone: Cross-modal structured transformer with grid target prediction (trained base, then continually updated with Dual-SR)
setting.training_data: R2R train for the base model (100k iterations, batch 20, lr 1e-5, 2 V100, 72 GPU hours); continual learning then runs 1k iterations per task domain on the validation splits (val seen/unseen) streamed by scene
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views with a topological graph of visited nodes
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (local plus global graph actions)
setting.privileged: Test-time continual updating: the agent is trained on the evaluation split's scenes as they stream in (with GT supervision on those tasks); evaluation follows the VLNCL protocol rather than a static test.

numbers.extra: Continual learning applied before evaluation; base agent (before CL) SR 43, SPL 37
numbers.evidence: Table 2: single-run performance on the test unseen split of R2R; Dual-SR(Ours) 17.90 4.54 65 59 51

numbers.extra: Max SR/OSR along the continual sequence, not the final value; Init SR 51.24, OSR 62.69
numbers.evidence: Table 4: tracking min/max SR and OSR; Dual-SR Max, Val Unseen 65.08 73.59

numbers_note: Test-unseen results are for a continually-updated agent and are not comparable to static single-run baselines. ST/UT values are reported in Table 3 (Dual-SR: Train Seen ST -8.49, Val Seen ST -6.00, Val Unseen UT 2.18).
results: On the R2R test unseen split, Dual-SR reaches SR 59 and SPL 51, compared with the base agent's 43 and 37 (+16 SR, +8 OSR). It is close to VLN-BERT's SR 57 and above the other listed baselines except SSM (SR 61). Versus plain fine-tuning, it gives clearly better ST and UT.
limitations: Only R2R is used and there is no ablation of the buffer, inner loop or outer loop; the comparison against prior CL methods is limited.

The baselines are compared under different conditions, since the CL agent adapts on the evaluation scenes, and the reported SR is a headline that mixes in the base agent's weak inference architecture.
Forgetting remains large: SR drops of up to about 20 points over 50 scenes.
builds_on: Jeong et al. continual VLN (PerpR, ESR)
